dossier:
**Source:** [Patwardhan et al., *GDPval: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Real-World Economically Valuable Tasks*](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.04374) (arXiv:2510.04374), §3.3–3.4 and App. A.2.6, A.3, A.6.4. The paper reports **aggregate evaluation of GPT-5 (high reasoning effort)** on the GDPval gold subset, not a single turn-by-turn trajectory.

---

### Task the agent was given

GDPval gold subset: **220 one-shot knowledge-work tasks** from industry experts (avg. ~14 years’ experience) across 44 occupations in the top 9 U.S. GDP sectors. Each task is a **request plus reference files** (up to 17 in gold; 67.7% of tasks have at least one). The required output is a **professional deliverable**—PDF, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, video, CAD, etc.—meant to match real occupational work. Expert completion time averages ~7–9 hours (up to weeks). Grading is **blind pairwise preference** by occupation experts vs. a human expert baseline (3 samples × 3 graders = 9 comparisons per task per model).

### Agent setup (baseline)

GPT-5 was run at **high reasoning effort** in a **custom harness**:

- **Web search** and **code interpreter**, with background sampling.
- A Docker container with a large preinstalled library set (App. A.6.4): document/PDF/slide tools (`python-pptx`, `python-docx`, `openpyxl`, `reportlab`, `weasyprint`, `PyMuPDF`, `pdf2image`, …), plus extra packages the prompt told the model it had (`libreoffice`, `aspose-words`, `cadquery`, etc.).
- No extra “check your own slides as images” instruction in the baseline prompt.

### What the agent did (baseline, as observed)

1. **Took the occupational request and references and produced file deliverables** via code interpreter (and web search when needed). OpenAI models were not sampled through a consumer UI the way Claude was; they used this tool-enabled container.

2. **Followed instructions and did calculations relatively well.** Clustering of expert justifications (§3.3 / Fig. 8) found GPT-5 high had the **fewest instruction-following failures** among GPT-5 high, Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Grok 4. GPT-5 and Grok had the fewest accuracy errors. GPT-5 **led on pure-text** deliverables; Claude led on `.pdf`, `.xlsx`, and `.ppt` (aesthetics/layout).

3. **Mostly did not inspect its own visual output.** Only **15%** of baseline GPT-5 runs used multimodal inspection of generated files (render pages/slides and look at them).

4. **Submitted PDFs and PowerPoints with systematic visual defects:**
   - **Black-square artifacts in more than half of generated PDFs.**
   - **Egregious formatting errors in 86% of PowerPoint files** (cut-off/overlapping/blank/distorted/low-contrast content).

5. **Still lost many head-to-heads to humans, mainly on formatting.** When experts preferred the human, GPT-5 high’s dominant loss reason was **formatting**, not missing files or ignored references (those were more Gemini/Grok). All models, including GPT-5, **sometimes hallucinated data or miscalculated**.

6. **Severity of those losses** (App. A.2.6, other experts re-rating GPT-5-vs-human losses): most often **“acceptable but subpar”** (usable but weaker than the human); **~29% “bad” or “catastrophic”**, of which **~3% catastrophic** (harmful/dangerously wrong: e.g. insulting a customer, wrong diagnosis, recommending fraud, suggesting physical harm); **~23% “model better”** (disagreement with the original grader, in line with inter-rater agreement). Win rates fell as expert completion time rose (best on 0–2 hour tasks).

### Intervention (the §3.4 / A.3 experiment)

Authors then changed scaffolding and added a **general** (not task-overfit) prompt (App. A.3):

- Avoid U+2011 and other special characters/emojis; use Noto fonts; **always create PDFs with LibreOffice**; keep diagrams large enough; keep deliverable text ≤4 sentences; put files in the container, not only in chat.
- **Mandatory pre-submit checks:** (1) convert visual files to per-page/slide PNGs with LibreOffice; (2) **display and inspect** those PNGs for cut-off, overlap, distortion, blanks, contrast; (3) programmatic checks (blank pages, overflow, slide limits); (4) match prompt instructions to the deliverable; (5) confirm exact files, reopen them. Repeat 1–5 if anything is wrong. End with `CONFIDENCE[XX]`.
- Scaffolding: **GET requests enabled in the container**; **best-of-N = 4** with a **GPT-5 judge** over prompt + references + four submissions.

### What changed after that

- Agents using **multimodal inspection: 15% → 97%**.
- **Black-square PDF artifacts: eliminated.**
- **Egregious PPT formatting errors: 86% → 64%** (still majority).
- **Human preference win rate: +5 percentage points** (Fig. 9(b)).
- Reasoning-effort sweep (low/medium/high) on o3 and GPT-5 also **raised performance** as effort increased (Fig. 9(a)).

### Final outcome

Baseline GPT-5 high, with web search + code interpreter, produced mostly instruction-faithful, relatively accurate work products, but **routinely shipped visually broken PDFs and slides** and **rarely looked at them**. After the A.3 prompt, GET access, and best-of-4 judging, visual self-checks became nearly universal, PDF black squares disappeared, PPT egregious errors fell but remained common (64%), and expert win rate rose 5 pp. Claude Opus 4.1 remained the overall gold-subset leader on aesthetics (47.6% win-or-tie vs. human).
